system_overview: This specification models the core algorithm of a model checker for state-based specifications, similar to the TLC model checker for TLA+. The algorithm takes a directed state graph with designated initial states and a set of violation states, then performs an exhaustive breadth-first exploration of all reachable states. If a violation state is found, the algorithm constructs a counterexample trace from an initial state to the violating state. If all states are explored without finding a violation, the algorithm reports success.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a single sequential model-checking process that explores a state graph. The inputs are: a directed graph with a set of states, a set of initial states, and a transition function mapping each state to its successor states; a set of violation states representing safety property violations; and a null value used as a placeholder.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) a FIFO queue of states awaiting exploration, initialized with a permutation of the initial states; (2) a set of already-explored states ensuring each state is visited at most once; (3) the current state being examined; (4) the set of unexplored successor states of the current state; (5) a loop counter for iterating through initial states; (6) a counterexample sequence that, when populated, contains a path from an initial state to a violating state; (7) a trace-back forest recording predecessor-successor pairs used to reconstruct the counterexample path; (8) a program counter tracking the algorithm's current phase.
initial_state: The exploration queue is initialized with one of the possible permutations of the initial states (modeling the fact that initial states have no defined order). The explored-states set is empty. The current state is null. The successor set is empty. The loop counter starts at one. The counterexample is an empty sequence. The trace-back forest is an empty sequence.
actions: The algorithm proceeds in four phases: (1) Initial state checking: iterate through the initial states in queue order, marking each as explored. If any initial state is a violation state, record it as the start of a counterexample and jump to trace reconstruction. (2) Post-initialization assertion: verify that all initial states have been explored. (3) Successor exploration: dequeue the next state, compute its unexplored successors. If the state has no successors at all (a deadlock), record it as a counterexample. Otherwise, for each unexplored successor: mark it as explored, enqueue it, record the predecessor-successor pair in the trace-back forest, and check whether it is a violation state. If it is, start trace reconstruction. If the queue becomes empty and no violation was found, assert that the violation set was empty and terminate successfully. (4) Trace reconstruction: starting from the violation state, repeatedly prepend the predecessor from the trace-back forest until an initial state is reached, producing the complete counterexample path.
liveness_properties: If violation states exist, the model checker eventually produces a counterexample: a non-empty sequence whose last element is a violation state and whose first element is an initial state. Termination: the algorithm eventually finishes exploring all states or finding a violation. The specification also checks that the algorithm terminates via a temporal property.
model_bounds: The state graph, violation states, and null value are declared as constants. For model checking, specific test graphs with known structures are used (defined in a companion test module). Graph sizes range from single-node graphs to 50-node graphs with various topologies.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the next-state relation, ensuring the algorithm makes progress. The specification is written using PlusCal syntax with a fair algorithm annotation. The exploration queue is initialized with a nondeterministic permutation of initial states because the order of initial states is undefined. The algorithm treats states with no outgoing transitions (other than self-loops) as deadlocked states. The trace-back forest stores predecessor-successor pairs as sequences of two-element sequences.
